h: Britain's Oldest Recorded Town on Your Doorstep
p: Colchester claims the title of Britain's oldest recorded town, and the story runs deep. It was Camulodunum, the first Roman capital of Britain, and Boudica's rebels burnt it to the ground in AD 60. That gives you a brilliant second day to pair with the zoo.

Colchester Castle sits at the heart of Castle Park and is a colossal Norman keep, built on the foundations of the Roman Temple of Claudius. Inside, the museum is packed with Roman finds and hands-on displays, and the vaults underneath are a properly atmospheric bit of history. Castle Park itself has gardens, play areas and stretches of the old Roman town wall still standing. The colourful Firstsite gallery is close by too, and the narrow lanes of the Dutch Quarter are worth a wander.

For coast, Mersea Island is a short drive south, reached by a causeway called the Strood that floods at the highest tides. It's famous for its oysters and beach huts. Or head north into Dedham Vale, the gentle river valley painted by John Constable, where Flatford Mill and the River Stour make a lovely calm afternoon.

At the zoo, the best tactic is to start early on one side of the site and work your way round rather than zigzagging. Staying until later in the afternoon can be rewarding, as the crowds thin and the animals often wake up again. Colchester has good rail links from London Liverpool Street, so a car isn't essential for exploring the town itself, though the zoo is easiest to reach by car or bus from the centre.
